name: Zhou 2025
question: Does intravaginal conjugated oestrogen improve continuation with satisfaction in postmenopausal women using a ring pessary for prolapse?

arms.label: Vaginal conjugated oestrogen cream with a ring pessary
placebo cream with a ring pessary

design.population: 420 postmenopausal women with symptomatic stage 2 or greater pelvic organ prolapse who successfully completed a two-week ring-pessary fitting trial at 12 Chinese hospitals.
design.description: Multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods (Study design, Participants, Randomisation and masking); Results (Baseline characteristics)

verdictNote: The 12-month continuation-with-satisfaction primary endpoint did not differ between groups.
takeaway: Adding intravaginal conjugated oestrogen cream rather than placebo cream to ring-pessary care did not improve 12-month continuation with patient-reported improvement in postmenopausal women with prolapse (181/208 versus 176/203; risk difference 0.3 percentage points, 95% CI −6.2 to 6.9).

reports.label: 12-month primary report
reports.citation: Zhou Y, Yin R, Zhang Y, et al. "Effects of intravaginal conjugated oestrogen on pessary continuation for pelvic organ prolapse: multicentre, randomised, double blind, placebo controlled trial." *BMJ.* 2025;389:e084418. doi:10.1136/bmj-2025-084418

results.measure: At 12 months, pessary use at least five days weekly plus PGI-I response of much better or very much better; risk difference in percentage points, oestrogen minus placebo, modified intention-to-treat
results.note: The trial was powered to detect a 14-percentage-point absolute difference; 411 of 420 randomized participants entered the modified intention-to-treat analysis.
results.locator: Full text, Methods (Outcomes, Statistical analysis); Results (Primary outcome), Table 2

results.measure: Pessary use at least five days weekly at 12 months; risk difference in percentage points, oestrogen minus placebo
results.note: Continuation is one component of the primary composite.

results.endpoint: Pessary continuation with satisfaction, per protocol
results.measure: 12-month composite among participants at least 50% adherent to cream for 12 months; risk difference in percentage points
results.note: Per-protocol sensitivity analysis; not the randomized primary analysis.

results.measure: Model-estimated change from baseline at 12 months; mean difference in points, oestrogen minus placebo
results.note: Both groups improved; between-group interval included zero.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 (Self-reported symptom improvement, one year)

harms.label: Any pessary-related adverse event
harms.note: Prespecified secondary safety outcome; risk difference −11.0 percentage points (95% CI −19.9 to −2.1).

harms.label: Excessive vaginal discharge
harms.note: Risk difference −9.3 percentage points (95% CI −17.1 to −1.4).

harms.label: Vaginal erosion or ulcer
harms.note: Risk difference −5.0 percentage points (95% CI −8.9 to −1.0).

harms.label: Vaginal bleeding
harms.note: Risk difference −5.0 percentage points (95% CI −8.7 to −1.2).

harms.label: Endometrial thickening on ultrasound
harms.note: Assessed at one year; difference was not statistically significant.

delivery.label: Cream regimen
delivery.value: 1 g of conjugated oestrogen cream (0.625 mg/g) or matching placebo vaginally nightly for two weeks, then twice weekly for 12 months.

delivery.label: Pessary fitting and self-care
delivery.value: A two-week trial of a ring pessary with support preceded randomization; participants or caregivers were taught to remove it at bedtime and reinsert it the next morning at least weekly.

delivery.label: Follow-up schedule
delivery.value: Visits every three months for one year, with telephone follow-up when an in-person visit was infeasible.

delivery.label: Modified intention-to-treat population
delivery.note: Four participants were completely lost to follow-up and five were found ineligible after randomization.
